extracted.intended_audience: life-science researchers, authors, reviewers, editors, and funders interested in preprints and peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing and using refereed (journal-independent) preprints: how peer review should assess manuscripts, and what qualities refereed preprints aim to deliver for authors, readers, editors and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the quality of a study
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should evaluate the quality of a study rather than judge suitability for a specific journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons 'asks reviewers to evaluate the quality of a study' — focusing on scientific rigor, validity of claims, and overall soundness instead of journal fit. Guidance implies focusing reviews on methodological correctness, interpretation, and whether conclusions follow from data, rather than perceived novelty for a particular journal audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess relevance for a particular scientific field
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess the work's relevance to its scientific field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform asks reviewers to evaluate 'its relevance for a particular scientific field rather than to determine whether the study is suitable for a specific journal.' Guidance: place the work in disciplinary context and judge importance/usefulness to specialists in that area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify flaws in design and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should detect poorly-done work and identify flaws in experimental design and data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article: 'Peer review ... can weed out poorly-done work, identify flaws in design and analysis and suggest improvements.' Reviews should check study design, controls, statistical methods, reproducibility, and point to concrete fixes or further experiments/analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive and rigorous reports (depth and rigour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should be constructive, detailed, and rigorous—offering actionable criticism and improvement suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece contrasts shallow comments on preprint servers with 'the depth and rigour offered by a formal peer-review process.' It warns against emotional or disruptive commentary common on social media and recommends focused, solution-oriented reviewer comments that help authors revise and readers assess quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Make peer-review materials (manuscript, referee report, authors' response) publicly available to increase transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons allows posting 'the manuscript, the referee report and the authors’ response' to bioRxiv or sharing with journals. Transparency guidance: public posting of reviews and responses enhances accountability and allows readers to see evaluation and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed / rapid dissemination while preserving review
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable rapid sharing of results via preprints while incorporating timely peer review to validate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints 'allow researchers to accelerate the sharing of information'; refereed preprints aim to combine speed with a 'thorough evaluation process.' Metrics cited: median time to posting of refereed preprints (71 days) and reduced time-to-publication (median 181 vs 253 days). Balance rapid dissemination with sufficient review depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundant peer-review cycles (transferability of reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide transferable, journal-agnostic referee reports so authors avoid repeated review cycles across journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons' model: after one round of peer review, reports can be transferred to partner journals, 'reducing the time that reviewers spend' and 'virtually eliminat[ing] repeated cycles.' Guidance: ensure reports are sufficiently general, thorough, and formatted so journals can reuse them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance readability, reliability, and overall research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereed preprints should improve a manuscript's readability, reliability, and scientific quality through reviewer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog states refereed preprints 'enhancing a preprint’s quality, reliability, and readability.' Reviews should include suggestions to clarify presentation, strengthen logic, and improve reproducibility and transparency to raise overall quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide usable guidance for journal selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports should help authors select a suitable journal for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article: 'The referee reports can help authors to select a suitable journal for their work, saving them the time spent reformatting and resubmitting.' Guidance: include assessment of audience/fit and recommend potential journal types or impact-level fits based on the work's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support funder and promotion assessment focusing on science not journal prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereed preprints should serve as indicators of research quality so evaluators can judge science independently of journal name or impact factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As more funders accept preprints, 'refereed preprints can also help those evaluating research to focus on the science rather than on the name or impact factor of the journal.' Guidance: reviews should be substantive enough that hiring/funding committees can rely on them as evidence of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify reviewer expertise and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reviewer credibility is discernible and conflicts of interest are managed or disclosed so readers can evaluate the trustworthiness of reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog notes difficulty on public comment platforms to 'discern the expertise and credibility of online commenters, as well as their potential conflicts of interest.' While Review Commons keeps reviewer identities confidential to journals, guidance implies documenting reviewers' domain qualifications or COI statements where appropriate to establish credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance efficiency with necessary time investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the review workflow to reduce redundant effort while recognizing peer review requires substantial time from authors, reviewers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes journal-based peer review 'requires a significant time investment' and estimates ~15 million hours spent on redundant reviews annually. Guidance: aim for one thorough, transferable review round to limit waste but preserve rigor; measure time-to-publication and reviewer burden as success metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against low-quality public commentary and emotional critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer formal peer review over unmoderated social-media commentary which can be emotional, disruptive, and of little help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contrasts rapid social-media debunking with its risks: 'this medium can also lead to emotional or disruptive comments which are of little help.' Guidance: encourage moderated, evidence-based commentary and discourage ad hominem or non-constructive posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider incentives, cost, and community adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Address practical adoption criteria: incentives for authors to post reviews, funding for refereed preprints, and community willingness to embrace transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog raises open questions: 'What incentives can encourage authors to publicly post the review process? Will funders cover the costs? Will the broader community embrace this level of transparency?' Guidance: plan funding models, credit systems, and cultural incentives to sustain refereed preprint services.
